newsitem.title: UK: BA says to sell Ground Fleet unit to Ryder.
newsitem.headline: BA says to sell Ground Fleet unit to Ryder.

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Tuesday it intended to sell its Ground Fleet Services division to Ryder Plc, a wholly owned subsidiary of Ryder System Inc of the U.S.

Ground Fleet currently employs 500 staff at Heathrow and Gatwick. It provides specialist ground equipment engineering and vehicle leasing services to operators at both airports and maintains a fleet of 7,300 vehicles.
Together with the sale, the airline intends to award Ryder a five-year contract at both Heathrow and Gatwick, subject to finalising a purchase agreement.
The sale forms part of British Airway's drive to improve services and reduce costs. The airline has targeted savings of one billion stg over the next three years from all parts of its operation.

"This announcement presents the best way forward for Ground Fleet Services and its employees, who will benefit from the focus and expertise of a company which specialises in this business," said British Airways chief executive Bob Ayling.
"This in turn will also benefit British Airways," he added.

Alternative studies had been undertaken to downsize the Ground Fleet Services division or create a separate profit centre within British Airways. The airline concluded that a third-party sale offered the best job security for the workforce and the greatest economic efficiency for the airline. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
